paragraphs: Fortrea Holdings Inc. is a leading global contract research organization ("CRO"), providing biopharmaceutical product and medical device development solutions to pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device customers. We provide phase I through IV clinical trial management, clinical pharmacology, and consulting services for our customers. For more than 30 years, we have supported our global pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device customers across more than 20 therapeutic areas, providing agile delivery models that include Full Service, Functional Service Provider ("FSP"), and Hybrid structures. We believe we are well positioned to leverage our global scale, scientific and therapeutic expertise, access to clinical data-driven insights, industry network, and decades of experience to bring customers distinctive, expert solutions.
Our team of approximately 14,300 employees is able to conduct operations in approximately 100 countries. Our solutions streamline the biopharmaceutical product and medical device development process.

Fortrea combines decades of domain expertise with the nimbleness required to meet market demand for flexible engagements with large and small customers, delivering solutions that bring life-changing treatments to patients faster and creating value for all stakeholders. Our expertise in the biopharmaceutical product and medical device development process has enabled us to design service offerings to better meet the needs of customers. We manage our business in one reporting segment — Clinical Services.

Fortrea Holdings Inc. was formed through a spin-off of the CRO business, which we refer to as the "Spin" or the "Separation," from Labcorp Holdings Inc., which we refer to herein as "Labcorp" or "Former Parent". All references in this Form 10-K to "Fortrea", "the Company", "we", "our" or "us" refer to Fortrea Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation, and its subsidiaries, unless otherwise indicated by the context. On June 29, 2023, which we refer to as the "Separation Date," Fortrea and Labcorp entered into a Separation and Distribution Agreement (the "Separation and Distribution Agreement"). Pursuant to the Separation and Distribution Agreement, Labcorp agreed to spin-off its CRO business into Fortrea, a standalone, publicly traded company. References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to "our consolidated and combined financial statements," "our combined financial statements" and similar expressions refer to the combined financial statements of Fortrea and Labcorp due to the fact that as of certain dates and during certain periods presented in the financial statements, Fortrea was still a wholly-owned subsidiary of, and operated under those businesses of, Labcorp.

On March 9, 2024, the Company, together with its wholly-owned subsidiary, Fortrea Inc., entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") with Endeavor Buyer LLC, an affiliate of Arsenal Capital Partners, to sell the operations of Fortrea Patient Access Inc. and its subsidiaries and Endpoint Clinical, Inc. and its subsidiaries; which are all collectively referred to as the Enabling Services Segment. The transaction closed during the second quarter of 2024. Refer to Note 3, "Discontinued Operations" to the audited consolidated and combined financial statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further discussion.

•Clinical Pharmacology. We are a recognized leader in clinical pharmacology, known for first-in-human and exploratory clinical pharmacology studies as well as biopharma label support studies. We offer an integrated clinical pharmacology solution that delivers with precision, quality and safety. Our solutions include our clinical research units ("CRUs") and external partnerships, project management, study design and monitoring, bioanalytics and biomarkers, pharmacokinetics ("PK"), modeling and simulation, and biometrics. Fortrea's CRUs are located in Leeds, U.K. offering 100 bed capacity; Dallas, Texas with 100 bed capacity; Daytona, Florida with 88 bed capacity; and Madison, Wisconsin with 88 bed capacity. Our offerings include deep expertise in areas such as radiolabeled absorption, metabolism and excretion studies, as well as studies involving normal healthy volunteer and patient populations. All Fortrea CRUs have current good manufacturing practice ("cGMP") pharmacies within them, enabling on-site manufacture of sterile and non-sterile drug product. A global bedside data capture system has been implemented across all CRUs, enabling increased efficiency and quality, and providing real time access to data.

•Clinical Development. We are a leading full-service provider of phase I through IV clinical and real-world evidence ("RWE") studies with a flexible approach to serving our customers. Clinical Development is Fortrea's largest offering in terms of annual revenue contribution and has been for the last five years. Services include, but are not limited to, regulatory affairs, protocol design, operational planning, study and site start-up, patient recruitment, project management, comprehensive site and medical monitoring, data management and biostatistics, pharmacovigilance, medical writing, and mobile clinical services. Our service offerings are supported by technological innovations, leveraging strategic relationships with leading technology vendors together with Fortrea's operational expertise to support more connected patient and site centric solutions, digital health and decentralized clinical trial capabilities. We are making focused investments in artificial intelligence ("AI"), machine learning ("ML"), other advanced technologies, and workflow automation and orchestration to drive speed, agility, quality and enhanced patient safety in clinical research. We focus on rapidly expanding research areas such as oncology, central nervous system and neurodegenerative, metabolic disorders including MASH (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis), immunology and inflammation (including autoimmune diseases and rheumatology), rare diseases, and cell and gene therapies. Additionally, we have deep scientific expertise in a broad spectrum of therapeutic areas and diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, nephrology (renal), infectious diseases, dermatology, ophthalmology, respiratory, and women's health, among others. For instance, during the period from January 2020 to December 2024, we conducted more than 5,930 phase I through IV clinical trial projects involving approximately 1,000,000 subjects. Clinical Development is enhanced by our pharmacology learnings, which we apply to future clinical programs. We also have a medical device and diagnostics offering, which has conducted more than 500 studies during that same period. We believe Fortrea is poised to capture additional market share in the large and expanding development market.
We offer our customers a tailored approach to clinical trial solutions through the use of three delivery models: Full Service, Functional Service Provider, and Hybrid.

◦Full Service. Integrates multiple disciplines from our service offerings to comprehensively support our customers in their development programs across key geographies. Our service offering integrates protocol design and operational planning, site start-up and patient recruitment, project and program management, comprehensive site and medical monitoring, centralized monitoring and medical data review, clinical and biometrics services, medical writing, and mobile clinical services. Our project-centric approach utilizes dynamic team resourcing with agile role-based structures. This approach allows for more adaptability to trial types with customer-tailored designs.

◦Functional Service Provider. Offers customers experienced personnel to perform targeted activities throughout their development programs. This approach reduces our customers' need to recruit and train dedicated internal resources which saves on cost and time and enables flexibility. Our service offering delivers comprehensive, strategic solutions designed to adapt to the level of customer control and infrastructure. Our FSP team can provide dedicated offerings in clinical operations, clinical data management, biostatistics, statistical programming, pharmacovigilance, mobile clinical services, and medical writing, among other customized solutions.

◦Hybrid. Provides the project-centric approach of a Full Service model while integrating FSP models to varying degrees on large portfolios with therapeutic similarities, to drive efficiencies and enhance sponsor control for clinical development. Our ability to tailor our services to customer needs demonstrates the agility we can offer customers across the industry value chain. Fortrea offers this flexibility at a global scale, and we are positioned as a partner of choice for customers that require a tailored approach.

•Consulting Services. We provide comprehensive consulting services from product development and regulatory strategy to market access and health economics and outcomes research ("HEOR"), including RWE services. Our teams provide expertise, innovation and support for all product development stages (nonclinical and clinical phases I-IV), for small and large molecules, cell and gene therapies and biosimilars, across multiple therapeutic areas, including rare diseases to help customers define the most appropriate stakeholder strategy, evidence generation, and development pathway to optimize productivity, value and outcomes for life science innovation.

CROs provide services to customers to assist in phase I through phase IV clinical trials and commercialization to accelerate the development of and access to safe, effective medical therapies and devices. Developing new biopharmaceutical products and medical devices for the treatment of human disease is a complex, costly, and lengthy process. Prior to commercialization, a biopharmaceutical product or medical device must undergo extensive preclinical and clinical testing as well as regulatory review to demonstrate an acceptable benefit-risk profile by regulatory authorities. As a result, bringing a new biopharmaceutical product to market takes about a decade1 and costs $2.23 billion on average.2

The biopharmaceutical product development process consists of three stages: preclinical, clinical, and commercialization. The preclinical process is the stage of research that begins prior to clinical studies and collects data on the feasibility, efficacy, and safety of drugs through experiments outside of the human body. The clinical stage is the most time-consuming and expensive part of the drug development process. During this stage, the product candidate undergoes a series of tests in humans. In phase I, small groups of study volunteers are exposed to ascending doses of the experimental product in order to assess safety and to determine the distribution of the drug and maximally tolerated dose. Preliminary assessment of the relationships between dosage, safety, and effectiveness follow in phase II before expanding to larger trials, phase III, to formally test effectiveness and safety in the target population. Phase IV, or post-approval trials, involves monitoring or verifying the risks and benefits of a drug product that has been approved and on the market.

headings: Risk Factor Summary
Risks Relating to Our Business
If we are unable to contract with suitable investigators and recruit and enroll patients for clinical trials, our business might suffer.
Our international operations could subject us to additional risks and expenses that could adversely impact our business or results of operations.
Embedded and functional outsourcing services associated with our FSP delivery models could subject us to employment liability, which may cause adverse effects on our business.
Our customer or therapeutic area concentrations may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.
Our customers may experience insufficient funding to complete their clinical trials.
Our backlog might not be indicative of our future revenues, and we might not realize all of the anticipated future revenue reflected in our backlog.
Increased competition, including price competition, could have a material adverse effect on our revenues and profitability.
An inability to attract and retain experienced and qualified personnel, including key management personnel, and increased personnel costs, could adversely affect our business.
We depend on third parties to provide services critical to our business and depend on them to comply with applicable laws and regulations.
If we are unable to effectively manage our growth, our business could be adversely affected.
Our relationships with existing or potential customers who are in competition with each other may adversely impact the extent to which those customers use our services.
Our business is dependent upon access to data and an inability to access the necessary data from our data partners on commercially reasonable terms or at all could adversely affect our business.
If we are unable to maintain effective internal controls, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows could be materially adversely affected.
Our brand, products or solutions may not be favorably received by our customers.
Epidemics, pandemics, or widespread public health crisis and associated economic repercussions, may have an adverse impact on our business and results of operations.
Our effective income tax rate may fluctuate, which may adversely affect our operations, earnings and earnings per share.
Risks Relating to Regulatory and Compliance Matters
Changes in government regulation or in practices relating to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical device industries could decrease the need for certain services that we provide.
Failure to comply with privacy and security laws and regulations could result in fines, penalties and damage to our reputation with customers and have a material adverse effect upon our business.
International operations may increase our exposure to liabilities under the anti-corruption laws.
Changes in and uncertainty regarding U.S. regulations, government policies, government funding decisions, trade policies or tariffs could have a material adverse effect upon our business.
Risks Relating to Strategic Transactions
paragraphs: The following are certain risk factors that could affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. The risks that are highlighted below are not the only risks that we face. Investors should carefully consider each of the following risks and all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. These risks relate to, among other things, our business and the industry in which we operate or to the securities markets generally and ownership of our common stock. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows could be negatively affected.

Below is a summary of the principal factors that make an investment in our common stock speculative or risky. This summary does not address all of the risks that we face. Additional discussion of the risks summarized in this risk factor summary, and other risks that we face, can be found below under the heading "Risk Factors" and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and our other filings with the SEC, before making an investment decision regarding our common stock.

•Our business, financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows may be materially adversely affected if we do not generate a large number of net new business awards, or if net new business awards are delayed, terminated, reduced in scope, or fail to go to contract.
•If we are unable to contract with suitable investigators and recruit and enroll patients for clinical trials, our business might suffer.
•Our international operations could subject us to additional risks and expenses that could adversely impact our business or results of operations.
•Our customer or therapeutic area concentrations may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis is intended to provide a summary of significant factors relevant to the financial performance and condition of Fortrea Holdings Inc., which we refer to in this discussion and analysis as "Fortrea," the "Company," "our" and "we". Prior to the spin-off which was completed on June 30, 2023 (the "Spin" or "the Separation"), Fortrea existed and functioned as part of Labcorp Holdings Inc., which we refer to in this discussion and analysis as "Labcorp" or "Former Parent." The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our audited consolidated and combined financial statements and corresponding notes and other financial information included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion contains forward-looking statements that are based upon current expectations and are subject to uncertainty and changes in circumstances. Our actual results could differ materially from the results contemplated by these forward-looking statements due to a number of factors, including those discussed below and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, particularly in Part I, Item 1A. "Risk Factors." Actual results may differ materially from these expectations. See "Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements."

Fortrea, a Delaware corporation incorporated on January 31, 2023, is a leading global contract research organization ("CRO") providing biopharmaceutical product and medical device development solutions to pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device customers. We offer customers highly flexible delivery models that include Full Service, Functional Service Provider ("FSP"), and Hybrid Service structures. We have a rich history of providing clinical development services for over 30 years across more than 20 therapeutic areas, first as Covance and later as Labcorp Drug Development. On June 30, 2023, we completed the Spin from Labcorp. We leverage our global scale, scientific and therapeutic expertise, clinical data insights, technology innovation, industry network and decades of experience as a standalone company and as a business unit prior to the Spin to deliver tailored solutions to our customers. With what we believe is a distinctive market offering, Fortrea meets growing global demand for clinical development services.

Our team of approximately 14,300 employees is able to conduct operations in approximately 100 countries and delivers comprehensive phase I – IV clinical trial management, clinical pharmacology, and consulting services for our customers. Our offering is scaled to deliver focused and agile solutions to customers globally, streamlining the biopharmaceutical product, and medical device development process.
For information about the industry outlook and markets that we operate in, refer to Part I, Item I. "Market Opportunity".

On June 30, 2023, we completed the Spin from Labcorp through a pro-rata distribution of one share of Fortrea common stock for every share of Labcorp common stock held at the close of business on the record date of June 20, 2023. Fortrea began to trade as a separate public company (NASDAQ: FTRE) on July 3, 2023.

The consolidated and combined statements of operations include costs for certain centralized functions and programs provided and administered by Labcorp that were allocated to us in the periods presented prior to the Spin. These centralized functions and programs include, but are not limited to, legal, tax, treasury, risk management, sales expenses, IT, human resources, finance, supply chain, executive leadership and stock-based compensation.

These expenses were allocated to us based on direct usage when identifiable or, when not directly identifiable, on the basis of proportional net revenues or headcount or another reasonable driver, as applicable. We consider the basis on which the expenses have been allocated to reasonably reflect the utilization of services provided to, or the benefit received by, us during the periods presented. However, the allocations may not reflect the expenses we would have incurred as an independent company for the periods presented and may not be representative of future expenses that may be incurred. Actual costs that may have been incurred if we had been a standalone company would depend on a number of factors, including the organizational structure, whether functions were outsourced or performed by employees, and strategic decisions made in areas such as IT and infrastructure. For a period following the Separation, however, some of these functions were provided by Labcorp under the Transition Services Agreement. The actual costs of services represented by these allocations may vary significantly from the amounts allocated to us in the accompanying financial statements.

On March 9, 2024, the Company, together with its wholly-owned subsidiary, Fortrea Inc. (the "Seller"), entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") with Endeavor Buyer LLC, an affiliate of Arsenal Capital Partners, pursuant to which the Seller agreed to sell, and to cause its affiliates to sell, certain assets relating to its Enabling Services Segment (the "Transaction"), including the sale of equity interests of Fortrea Patient Access Inc. and its subsidiaries and Endpoint Clinical, Inc. and its subsidiaries. The final adjusted purchase price for the Transaction was $340.0, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, with $295.0 paid at closing and $45.0 to be paid upon achievement of certain transition-related milestones, which includes certain services provided through a Transition Services Agreement. The Transaction closed during the second quarter of 2024. The first milestone payment in the amount of $20.0 was received in the first quarter of 2025. The second and final milestone payment in the amount of $25.0 was received in the third quarter of 2025. The Transaction resulted in a loss on disposal of $19.6. The decision to sell such assets relating to the Enabling Services Segment represented a strategic shift that had a significant effect on the Company's results and operations for the periods presented. As a result, the operations of the Enabling Services Segment have been classified as loss from discontinued operations on the consolidated and combined statements of operations.

Our backlog consists of anticipated future revenue from business awards that either have not started, or that are in process and have not been completed. Our backlog also reflects any cancellation or adjustment activity related to these awards. The average duration of our contracts will fluctuate from period to period based on the contracts comprising our backlog at any given time. The majority of our contracts contain early termination provisions that typically require notice periods ranging from 30 to 90 days. We adjust backlog for foreign currency fluctuations and exclude from backlog amounts that have been recognized as revenue in our statements of operations. Our backlog was $7.7 billion as of December 31, 2025.

We do not believe that, as a sole measure, our backlog is a consistent indicator of future revenue because it has been, and likely will continue to be, affected by a number of factors, including the variable size and duration of projects, many of which are performed over several years, and changes to the scope of work during the course of projects. Additionally, projects may be canceled or delayed by the customer or regulatory authorities. We generally do not have a contractual right to the full amount of the contract award reflected in our backlog. If a customer cancels a contract, we generally will be reimbursed for the costs we have incurred. For more information about risks related to our backlog see "Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our Business—Our backlog might not be indicative of our future revenues, and we might not realize all of the anticipated future revenue reflected in our backlog."

The change in revenues was due to an increase in organic revenues of 0.8%, and favorable foreign currency translation of 0.2%. The Company defines organic growth as the change in revenues excluding the year over year impact of acquisitions, divestitures and currency. The 0.8% increase in organic revenues was primarily driven by an increase in revenue in our clinical pharmacology business, including higher pass through costs. This increase was partially offset by lower clinical development revenues resulting primarily from the mix of complex and longer duration studies in our portfolio as well as lower functional service provider revenue, which more than offset revenue from net new business, including higher pass through costs as projects progress through their lifecycle.

paragraphs: Fortrea Holdings Inc. 為全球領先的合同研究組織（"CRO"），為製藥、生物科技與醫療器材客戶提供生物製藥產品與醫療器材開發解決方案。我們為客戶提供第 I 至第 IV 階段臨牀試驗管理、臨牀藥理學與諮詢服務。在超過 30 年的時間裡，我們已支持全球製藥、生物科技與醫療器材客戶，涵蓋超過 20 種治療領域，提供包含完整服務、功能服務供應商（"FSP"）與混合結構的靈活交付模式。我們相信我們已具備優勢，能善用全球規模、科學與治療專業知識、臨牀數據驅動的洞察力、產業網路與數十年經驗，為客戶提供獨特且專業的解決方案。
我們約 14,300 名員工的團隊，能在約 100 個國家進行運作。我們的解決方案可簡化生物製藥產品與醫療器材的開發流程。
Fortrea 將數十年的領域專業知識與市場對靈活合作需求的靈活性結合，為大型與小型客戶提供解決方案，使患者能更快獲得改變生命的治療，並為所有利害關係人創造價值。我們在生物製藥產品與醫療器材開發流程的專業知識，使我們能設計服務方案，以更符合客戶需求。我們將業務管理為一個應報告分部 — 臨牀服務。

Fortrea Holdings Inc. 是透過從 Labcorp Holdings Inc.（我們 herein 稱為 "Labcorp" 或 "Former Parent"）分拆出的 CRO 事業所成立，我們稱此為 "Spin" 或 "Separation"。本 Form 10-K 中所有提及 "Fortrea"、"the Company"、"we"、"our" 或 "us" 的參考，均指 Fortrea Holdings Inc.，一家 Delaware 公司及其子公司，除非上下文另有說明。於 2023 年 6 月 29 日（我們稱為 "Separation Date"），Fortrea 與 Labcorp 籤訂了分拆與發行協議（"Separation and Distribution Agreement"）。根據分拆與發行協議，Labcorp 同意將其 CRO 事業分拆至 Fortrea，一家獨立上市的公司。本年度報告 Form 10-K 中提及 "我們合併與合併財務報表"、"我們合併財務報表" 及類似表達，均指 Fortrea 與 Labcorp 的合併財務報表，因為在財務報表中所提及的某些日期與期間，Fortrea 仍為 Labcorp 的 wholly-owned 子公司，並在 Labcorp 的業務下運作。

2024 年 3 月 9 日，本公司與其 wholly-owned 子公司 Fortrea Inc. 與 Endeavor Buyer LLC（Arsenal Capital Partners 的附屬公司）簽訂資產買賣協議（"Purchase Agreement"），出售 Fortrea Patient Access Inc. 及其子公司與 Endpoint Clinical, Inc. 及其子公司之運作，這些皆 collectively 稱為 Enabling Services Segment。交易於 2024 年第二季完成。有關進一步討論，請參閱 Part II, Item 8 本年度報告 Form 10-K 中的 Note 3，"Discontinued Operations"。

•臨牀藥理學。我們是臨牀藥理學領域的知名領導者，以首例人體臨牀與探索性臨牀藥理學研究以及生物製藥標籤支援研究聞名。我們提供整合的臨牀藥理學解決方案，以精準、品質與安全性為導向。我們的解決方案包括臨牀研究單位（"CRUs"）、外部合作夥伴、專案管理、研究設計與監測、生物分析與生物標記物、藥動學（"PK"）、建模與模擬，以及生物統計學。Fortrea 的 CRUs 位於 Leeds, U.K.，提供 100 張病牀容量；Dallas, Texas，提供 100 張病牀容量；Daytona, Florida，提供 88 張病牀容量；以及 Madison, Wisconsin，提供 88 張病牀容量。我們的解決方案包括在放射性標記吸收、代謝與排除研究，以及涉及正常健康志願者與患者羣體的研究方面的深度專業知識。所有 Fortrea CRUs 均設有符合良好製造規範（"cGMP"）的藥房，使現場製造無菌與非無菌藥品成為可能。我們已在所有 CRUs 中實施全球牀邊數據捕捉系統，提高效率與品質，並提供即時數據存取。

•臨牀開發。我們是提供第 I 至第 IV 階段臨牀與真實世界證據（"RWE"）研究的領先全服務供應商，並以靈活的方式服務客戶。臨牀開發是 Fortrea 最主要的服務項目，以年度營收貢獻而言，已連續五年為最大。服務包括但不限於：法規事務、協議設計、運營規劃、研究與場地啟動、受試者招募、專案管理、全面場地與醫療監測、數據管理與生物統計學、藥物不良反應監測、醫療寫作與移動臨牀服務。我們的服務方案由科技創新支撐，結合與領先科技供應商的戰略合作關係與 Fortrea 的運營專業知識，以支持更連接的患者與場地中心解決方案、數位健康與分散式臨牀試驗能力。我們正專注投資於人工智慧（"AI"）、機器學習（"ML"）、其他先進科技與工作流程自動化與協調，以加速臨牀研究的速度、靈活性、品質與提升患者安全。我們專注於快速擴展的研究領域，例如癌症、中樞神經系統與神經退化、代謝疾病包括 MASH（代謝功能異常相關脂肪肝炎）、免疫學與發炎（包括自身免疫疾病與風濕病學）、罕見疾病以及細胞與基因治療。此外，我們在廣泛的治療領域與疾病方面擁有深厚的科學專業知識，例如心血管疾病、腎臟病學（腎臟）、感染性疾病、皮膚科、眼科、呼吸系統與婦女健康，等等。例如，在 2020 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月期間，我們進行了超過 5,930 個第 I 至第 IV 階段臨牀試驗專案，涉及約 1,000,000 名受試者。臨牀開發因我們的藥理學知識而得到提升，我們將這些知識應用於未來的臨牀計畫。我們也擁有醫療器材與診斷服務，該服務在相同期間內已進行超過 500 個研究。我們相信 Fortrea 有機會在這個龐大且持續成長的開發市場中，進一步取得市場份額。
我們透過使用三種交付模式：完整服務、功能服務供應商與混合模式，為客戶提供量身打造的臨牀試驗解決方案。
◦完整服務。整合多種專業領域，從我們的服務方案中全面支持客戶在其關鍵地理區域的開發計畫。我們的服務方案整合協議設計與作業規劃、場地啟動與受試者招募、專案與計畫管理、全面場地與醫療監測、集中監測與醫療資料審查、臨牀與生物測量服務、醫療寫作，以及行動臨牀服務。我們以專案為中心的作法，運用動態的團隊資源配置與敏捷的職能結構。此作法使我們能更靈活地適應不同類型的試驗，並根據客戶需求進行設計。
◦功能性服務提供者。為客戶提供經驗豐富的專業人員，執行其開發計畫中的特定活動。此作法減少客戶招募與培訓專屬內部資源的需求，節省成本與時間，並提升靈活性。我們的服務方案提供全面且戰略性的解決方案，以適應客戶控制程度與基礎設施的層級。我們的FSP團隊可提供專屬的臨牀作業、臨牀資料管理、生物統計、統計程式設計、藥物不良反應監測、行動臨牀服務與醫療寫作等服務，以及其他客製化解決方案。
◦混合模式。提供完整服務模式的專案中心作法，同時根據大型且具有治療相似性的組合，整合不同程度的FSP模式，以提高效率並增強贊助方對臨牀開發的控制力。我們能根據客戶需求調整服務方案的能力，展現我們在產業價值鏈中所能提供的靈活性。Fortrea在全球規模提供此種靈活性，我們被定位為需要客製化方案客戶的首選合作夥伴。

•諮詢服務。我們提供從產品開發與法規策略到市場准入與健康經濟與結果研究（"HEOR"），包括實證研究（RWE）服務的全面諮詢服務。我們的團隊提供專業知識、創新與支援，協助客戶在所有產品開發階段（非臨牀與臨牀階段I-IV），包括小分子與大分子、細胞與基因治療及生物類似藥品，於多個治療領域，包括罕見疾病，協助客戶定義最適當的利害關係人策略、證據產生與開發路徑，以優化生產力、價值與結果，促進生命科學創新。
CROs 提供服務給客戶，協助進行第一期至第四期臨牀試驗及商品化，以加速安全、有效的醫療療法與醫療器材的開發與取得。開發新的生物製藥產品與醫療器材用以治療人類疾病是一個複雜、成本高昂且耗時的過程。在商品化之前，生物製藥產品或醫療器材必須經過廣泛的預臨牀及臨牀測試以及法規審查，以向法規機關證明其可接受的效益-風險評估。因此，將新生物製藥產品推向市場約需十年1，平均成本為 2.23 十億美元2。

生物製藥產品開發過程包含三個階段：非臨牀、臨牀與商業化。非臨牀階段是研究階段，開始於臨牀試驗之前，透過體外實驗收集藥物的可行性、療效與安全性資料。臨牀階段是藥物開發過程中耗時且成本最高的階段。在此階段，產品候選物會進行一系列的人體測試。在第I期，小組試驗志願者會接觸逐步增加劑量的實驗性產品，以評估安全性並確定藥物的分佈與最大耐受劑量。第II期會進一步評估劑量、安全性與療效的關係，然後擴展至較大的試驗，即第III期，以正式測試產品在目標人羣中的療效與安全性。第IV期，或稱為上市後試驗，則涉及監測或驗證已批准並上市的藥物產品的風險與效益。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析旨在提供與 Fortrea Holdings Inc. 財務表現與狀況相關的重要因素總結，我們在本討論與分析中稱為 "Fortrea"、"本公司"、"我們" 及 "我們"。在 2023 年 6 月 30 日完成分拆前（稱為 "分拆" 或 "分離"），Fortrea 作為 Labcorp Holdings Inc. 的一部分存在並運作，我們在本討論與分析中稱為 "Labcorp" 或 "原母公司"。以下對我們財務狀況與營運結果的討論與分析應與我們經審計的合併及合併財務報表及其相關附註，以及其他財務資訊一同閱讀。本討論包含基於當前預期的展望性陳述，並受不確定性及情況變化的影響。我們實際結果可能與這些展望性陳述所預期的結果有重大差異，原因包括下列所討論的及其他在本年度報告 10-K 中提及的因素，特別是在第一部分，第 1A 項 "風險因素"。實際結果可能與這些預期有重大差異。請參閱 "關於展望性陳述的警示聲明"。

Fortrea 是一間於 2023 年 1 月 31 日在特拉華州註冊的公司，為全球領先的合同研究組織（"CRO"），為藥品、生物科技及醫療器材客戶提供生物藥物產品及醫療器材開發解決方案。我們為客戶提供高度靈活的交付模式，包括全服務、功能服務供應商（"FSP"）及混合服務結構。我們有超過 30 年的臨牀開發服務經驗，涵蓋超過 20 種治療領域，最初為 Covance，後為 Labcorp Drug Development。2023 年 6 月 30 日，我們完成從 Labcorp 的分拆。我們利用全球規模、科學及治療專業知識、臨牀數據洞察、科技創新、產業網路及數十年的獨立公司及作為業務單位的經驗，為客戶提供量身打造的解決方案。我們相信擁有獨特的市場提供方案，Fortrea 滿足全球對臨牀開發服務日益增長的需求。
我們約 14,300 名員工團隊能在約 100 個國家進行運作，為客戶提供從一期至四期的臨牀試驗管理、臨牀藥理學及諮詢服務。我們的服務規模足以在全球為客戶提供專注且靈活的解決方案，簡化生物藥物產品及醫療器材開發流程。
有關產業展望及我們運作的市場資訊，請參閱第一部分，第 I 項 "市場機會"。
2023 年 6 月 30 日，我們透過按比例發放 Fortrea 普通股，完成從 Labcorp 的分拆，每持有 Labcorp 普通股一股，發放 Fortrea 普通股一股。Fortrea 於 2023 年 7 月 3 日開始以獨立公開公司（納斯達克：FTRE）交易。
合併及合併營運狀況陳述包含由 Labcorp 提供並管理的某些集中功能及計畫的成本，這些成本在分拆前已按期間分配至我們。這些集中功能及計畫包括，但不僅限於，法律、稅務、財務、風險管理、銷售費用、資訊科技、人力資源、財務、供應鏈、高階領導及股票薪酬。

這些費用根據直接使用情況進行分配，若無法識別則根據比例淨銷售額或人數或其他合理指標進行分配。我們認為費用分配的基礎能合理反映我們在期間內使用服務或獲得的利益。然而，這些分配可能無法反映我們作為獨立公司期間實際產生的費用，也可能不具代表性未來可能產生的費用。如果我們為獨立公司，實際產生的成本將取決於多種因素，包括組織結構、功能是否委外或由員工執行，以及在資訊科技及基礎設施等領域的戰略決策。然而，在分離後的一段期間內，部分功能由 Labcorp 透過過渡服務協議提供。這些分配所代表的服務成本可能與財務報表中分配給我們的金額有顯著差異。

2024 年 3 月 9 日，本公司與其全資子公司 Fortrea Inc.（"賣方"）與 Endeavor Buyer LLC（Arsenal Capital Partners 的附屬公司）簽訂資產買賣協議（"買賣協議"），賣方同意出售與其 Enabling Services 分部（"交易"）相關的資產，包括 Fortrea Patient Access Inc. 及其子公司與 Endpoint Clinical, Inc. 及其子公司的股權。交易的最終調整後買價為 340.0 美元，根據常規買價調整，其中 295.0 美元於交易完成時支付，45.0 美元於達成某些過渡相關里程碑時支付，包括透過過渡服務協議提供的某些服務。交易於 2024 年第二季完成。第一筆里程碑付款 20.0 美元於 2025 年第一季收到。第二筆及最終里程碑付款 25.0 美元於 2025 年第三季收到。交易導致處置損失 19.6 美元。出售與 Enabling Services 分部相關資產的決定代表一項戰略轉變，對本公司在報告期間的結果及營運產生重大影響。因此，Enabling Services 分部的營運已歸類為合併及合併營運狀況陳述中的已終止營運損失。
我們的待執行訂單包含預期未來營業收入，來自尚未開始或正在進行但尚未完成的業務契約。待執行訂單也反映與這些契約相關的任何取消或調整活動。我們契約的平均執行期間會根據每個期間內組成待執行訂單的契約而有所變動。我們大多數契約包含提前終止條款，通常需要30至90天的通知期。我們會根據外幣波動調整待執行訂單，並排除已認列為收入的金額。我們的待執行訂單為2025年12月31日為止為7.7十億美元。

我們不認為待執行訂單單獨作為指標，能一致反映未來收入，因為它已受到多種因素的影響，包括專案的變動規模與執行期間，許多專案執行期間長達數年，以及專案執行過程中的工作範疇變動。此外，專案可能因客戶或監管機關的取消或延遲而中止。我們通常沒有契約權利取得待執行訂單中反映的全部契約金額。若客戶取消契約，我們通常會獲得已發生成本的補償。如需更多有關待執行訂單相關風險資訊，請參閱「風險因素—與我們業務相關的風險—我們的待執行訂單可能無法反映未來收入，且我們可能無法實現待執行訂單中反映的全部預期未來收入。」
以下為管理層對財務狀況與營運結果的分析，旨在協助您瞭解我們2025年及2024年12月31日財務年度的營運結果。如需比較我們2024年及2023年財務年度的營運結果，請參閱我們2024年財務年度12月31日年度報告（Form 10-K）的「第二部分，第7項 管理層對財務狀況與營運結果的分析」，該報告已於2025年3月3日提交至證券交易委員會。
以下表格呈現管理層認為最能反映本公司營運績效的重要財務指標。

2024 $ 2,723.4 $ 2,696.4 % 本公司2025年12月31日財務年度的營業收入為2,723.4，較2024年同期的2,696.4增加1.0%。營業收入的變動主要由於有機營收增加0.8%，以及有利的外幣匯兌影響0.2%。本公司將有機成長定義為排除年對年收購、出售及外幣影響後的營收變動。有機營收增加0.8%主要是由於我們臨牀藥理學業務的營收增加，包括更高的過渡成本。此增加部分抵銷了臨牀開發營收的下降，主要由於我們產品組閤中複雜且執行期間較長的專案比例，以及功能性服務提供者營收的下降，這已超過新業務帶來的營收，包括隨著專案進程而增加的過渡成本。

headings: 風險因素總覽
與我們業務相關的風險
